title: A countable submodule can be adapted to a scalar-extension direct sum
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $L$ be an $A$-module. Suppose a $B$-linear isomorphism $\theta:B\otimes_A L\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i$ is given [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], where $I$ is a set and every $Q_i$ is a countably generated $B$-module. If $C\subseteq L$ is a countably generated $A$-submodule, there exist a countably generated $A$-submodule $P\subseteq L$ with $C\subseteq P$ and a subset $J\subseteq I$ such that $\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A P\to B\otimes_A L))=\bigoplus_{j\in J}Q_j$, viewed as the coordinate submodule of $\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i$. Countably generated means that an at most countable subset spans by finite linear combinations. The tensor map is induced by $P\hookrightarrow L$, and the $B$-action is through the left tensor factor. No flatness or projectivity is assumed.

proof.text: Set $N_0=C$. Inductively suppose $N_\ell\subseteq L$ is countably generated and let $E_\ell=\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A N_\ell\to B\otimes_A L))$. Let $I_\ell$ be the set of indices $i$ for which the $i$-th coordinate projection of $E_\ell$ is nonzero. A countable generating family for $N_\ell$ gives countably many pure tensors, and each pure tensor has finite coordinate support in the direct sum, so $I_\ell$ is countable. Consequently $Q_\ell=\bigoplus_{i\in I_\ell}Q_i$ is countably generated: choose countable generators in each $Q_i$ and enumerate the resulting countable union. The tensor and direct-sum definitions justify these finite-support and generation assertions.

source.place: Tag 05A8, proof, first paragraph (construction of N'_ell and I'_ell)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-lift-countably-generated-submodule] to the countably generated $B$-submodule $Q_\ell\subseteq B\otimes_A L$. It gives a countably generated $A$-submodule $P_\ell\subseteq L$ whose tensor image contains $Q_\ell$. Define $N_{\ell+1}=N_\ell+P_\ell$. It is countably generated, contains $N_\ell$, and its tensor image contains every $Q_i$ with $i\in I_\ell$, exactly as required for the next stage.

source.place: Tag 05A8, proof, first paragraph (apply Tag 05A7 and set N'_{ell+1}=N'_ell+P)

proof.text: Iterate the preceding construction over $\ell=0,1,2,\ldots$, and put $P=\bigcup_{\ell\ge0}N_\ell$ and $J=\bigcup_{\ell\ge0}I_\ell$. The union $P$ is an $A$-submodule containing $C$ and is countably generated by taking the union of the countable generating families chosen at the stages. If $i\in J$, then $i\in I_\ell$ for some $\ell$, so $Q_i\subseteq E_{\ell+1}$ and hence $\bigoplus_{i\in J}Q_i$ is contained in the image $E=\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A P\to B\otimes_A L))$. Conversely, any tensor element from $B\otimes_A P$ is a finite sum of pure tensors, so its finitely many elements of $P$ lie in one common $N_\ell$; its image therefore lies in $E_\ell$ and has coordinates only in $I_\ell\subseteq J$. Thus $E\subseteq\bigoplus_{j\in J}Q_j$.

source.place: Tag 05A8, proof, final paragraph (take the union and identify I' = union I'_ell)

proof.text: Applying the given isomorphism $\theta$ to the equality in Step 3 yields $\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A P\to B\otimes_A L))=\bigoplus_{j\in J}Q_j$ as the coordinate submodule of $\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i$. This is the claimed adapted submodule, with no flatness or projectivity used.
